validity.researcher_notes: This is Williams' Northwest Pipeline LLC interstate transmission SYSTEM row (not a single project/segment), and it is real, currently operating, and correctly classified. Existence + classification confirmed independently: Williams' own site (williams.com/pipeline/northwest-pipeline/) describes an approximately 3,900-mile bi-directional interstate transmission system; Rextag (third-party pipeline-data vendor, rextag.com/pages/northwest-pipeline) independently lists 'Miles of Pipeline: 3900' and 'System Capacity: 3.8 Bcf/d'; and Williams' FY2025 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, filed 2026-02-24, joint Williams/Transco/NWP annual report, CIK 0000110019 for Northwest Pipeline LLC) states in Item 1 Business: 'NWP owns and operates an approximately 3,900-mile natural gas pipeline system, extending from the San Juan basin in northwestern New Mexico and southwestern Colorado through Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, Oregon, and Washington to a point on the Canadian border near Sumas, Washington... NWP's principal business is the interstate transportation of natural gas, which is regulated by the FERC' -- confirming both existence and the 'transmission' classification (FERC-regulated interstate transmission, not gathering/distribution). The 10-K also states NWP is a wholly owned subsidiary of Williams (confirming Owner1 = Williams Companies, 100%). No duplicate risk: P0230 is correctly the aggregate system row, distinct from the roster's other Northwest Pipeline entries, which are genuine sub-projects on this same system -- P2626 (Trail West/N-MAX, cancelled), P5101 (Kalama Lateral, cancelled), P7790 (Kelso-Beaver Reliability Project, proposed) and P7812 (Wild Trail project, proposed); EIA's Aug 2026 Natural Gas Pipeline Projects release independently corroborates both P7790 (capacity 183 MMcf/d, sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', Excel row 69, docket CP25-89, status Approved) and P7812 (capacity ~83 MMcf/d [82.955], Excel row 136, docket CP25-497-000, status Approved) exactly against the roster's recorded capacities -- filed as cross_row_leads below. The same Aug 2026 EIA release also shows several very recent/ongoing NWP system expansions not present anywhere in this 42-row roster (Huntingdon Connector, CP26-94, Applied, Sumas WA receipt point, 87 MMcf/d, Excel row 66; Naughton Coal-to-Gas Conversion, WY, Construction/near-complete, Excel row 86; Ryckman Creek Lateral Loop, WY, Applied, Excel row 104; Stanfield South Project, OR-ID, placed in service 2025-09-30, Excel row 1200) -- these may be undiscovered rows for a future Discovery pass on this system; noted here for the orchestrator, not researched further (out of this row's scope). One caveat filed separately below: StartYear1 (1965) could not be corroborated by any source found and independent evidence suggests it may be a data error.

validity.recommendation: Re-verify StartYear1 (1965) against a primary source (FERC's original 1950s certificate for the system's predecessor, Pacific Northwest Pipeline Corporation) or clear it if none can be found.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's cited ref for Start (williams.com/pipeline/northwest-pipeline/) does not state 1965 or any other year anywhere on the page (confirmed by direct read; the builder's own existing_ref_check already flagged this as a value-not-found FAIL). Williams' FY2025 10-K likewise gives no founding/in-service year for NWP. Independent secondary evidence argues against 1965 being correct: Encyclopedia.com's International Directory of Company Histories entry on The Williams Companies, Inc. states Williams acquired the Great Lakes pipeline network (an unrelated, 6,228-mile system) in 1965, and separately acquired Northwest Pipeline (this system) only in 1983 -- 'that same year Williams acquired two natural gas pipelines: Northwest pipeline, which served the West Coast, and Northwest Central, which was located in the Midwest.' Since GEM's StartYear1 records when the pipeline began commercial operation (not when Williams bought it), and the system's actual construction/first-gas predates the 1983 Williams acquisition by decades (built by predecessor Pacific Northwest Pipeline Corporation in the 1950s per general industry history), 1965 fits neither the true founding date nor the Williams-acquisition date -- it plausibly is a conflation with the unrelated 1965 Great Lakes transaction. I could not locate a primary source (FERC docket, PHMSA record, or dated trade history) stating the system's actual in-service year within this pass's search budget (WebSearch quota was exhausted mid-sweep; DuckDuckGo HTML search and several guessed corporate-history URLs -- williams.com/about-us/our-history/, fundinguniverse.com, historylink.org -- 404'd or gave no date). Recommend a follow-up pass with FERC eLibrary docket search for the original 1950s certificate rather than treating 1965 as confirmed.
